points: Q3 revenue will show whether the 12% Q2 growth was mostly a one-time lift from New York City camera installations and bus-lane expansion; a slowdown would fit the 8.5% revenue estimate cut and seven analyst downgrades over the past month.

Q2 swung to a $48.2 million net loss because of goodwill and intangible impairments plus a prior-period tax reserve release; Q3 will reveal whether those charges are truly one-off or if underlying earnings are eroding ahead of the 13.6% expected FY1 EPS decline.

Operating cash flow dropped to $56.4 million in Q2 from $75.1 million a year ago; Q3 cash generation will show whether cash conversion is weakening even though adjusted EBITDA rose, which would hurt earnings quality.
Management revised FY2026 guidance in Q2; the Q3 print and updated outlook will test whether that guidance is already at risk, given consensus expects FY2 EPS to fall another 16.9%.

Commercial Services grew 6% in Q2 on RAC tolling and higher violations processing, and reports suggest Avis sent a termination notice earlier in 2026; Q3 will clarify whether the Avis and Hertz extensions are producing stable, durable revenue or if customer concentration risk is rising.

Parking Solutions added only $0.2 million in Q2 as SaaS gains were offset by lower subscription and professional services; Q3 will show if that segment is still shrinking, which would weigh on overall growth.

The forward P/E is roughly 0.2x the sector median, so the market is already pricing the forecasted FY1 and FY2 EPS declines; Q3 will show whether that deep discount is a value trap or a real turnaround.
watch: Q3 revenue growth decelerating from Q2's 12% supports the short.
Q3 operating cash flow staying below the year-ago $75.1 million level supports the short.
Adjusted EBITDA margin failing to expand or declining supports the short.
FY2026 guidance being maintained rather than raised, or lowered, supports the short.
